h1: CNC plasma tables and CNC plasma pipe cutting machines
intro: A CNC plasma table cuts steel, stainless and aluminum plate to any shape from a drawing — brackets, gussets, base plates, signs and art — at a fraction of the price of a laser, and cuts thicker plate than a small laser. NovoTech's value-line plasma machines are built in China to our specification: industrial 4 × 4 and 5 × 10 ft tables with servo drives, automatic torch height control and water or downdraft tables, compact 2 × 2 and 2 × 4 ft tables that run from a USB stick, and CNC plasma pipe cutters that cope and saddle pipe from Ø2 to 11-3/4″. Supplied with the plasma source or ready for a Hypertherm; installed and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.a: A plasma table costs much less, cuts thicker plate for the money and is simple to run; its cut is wider with a slight bevel and some dross, which is fine for structural, agricultural and repair work. A fiber laser cuts thin and medium sheet faster with a narrow, square, clean edge and small holes — the choice for sheet-metal parts and enclosures. See the fiber laser cutting machines page for the laser line-up.

The plasma source sets the thickness, not the table: a 45 A source cuts about 5/16″ cleanly, 65 A 3/8″, 85 A 1/2″, 100 A 1″ (severance). The 4×4 and 5×10 tables carry plate up to 1″ thick. Tell us your usual and thickest plate and we will match the source.

A water table catches the sparks and most of the fumes in water under the plate — simple and quiet; a downdraft table draws the fumes down through the slats into a dust collector and keeps the plate dry. The 4×4 table cuts over water pans, the 5×10 has downdraft collection.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
